examples.claim: Supported hardware: NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Intel XPU, Apple Silicon via vLLM-Metal, several CPU architectures; vllm serve starts an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8000
examples.source: installation/README.md hardware list; quickstart.md L209 'By default, it starts the server at http://localhost:8000'.

examples.claim: Blog measured LLaMA-7B on A10G and LLaMA-13B on A100 40GB with ShareGPT-sampled input/output lengths
examples.source: blog: 'two settings: LLaMA-7B on an NVIDIA A10G GPU and LLaMA-13B on an NVIDIA A100 GPU (40GB). We sample the requests' input/output lengths from the ShareGPT dataset.'

examples.claim: CacheConfig.block_size accepts None (use default) and is always an int after construction; v0.10.0 docs said CUDA supports block sizes up to 32 only
examples.source: cache.py L188-L190 docstring; v0.10.0 config.py L1620-L1621 'On CUDA devices, only block sizes up to 32 are supported.'

examples.claim: A 300-token request with block size 16 needs ceil(300/16)=19 blocks, 304 slots, 4 empty
examples.source: Arithmetic: 300/16 = 18.75 -> 19; 19×16 = 304; 304-300 = 4. Mechanism per arXiv §4.3 'limits all the memory wastes for a request within one block'.

examples.claim: Memory sharing cuts parallel sampling and beam search memory by up to 55% and raises throughput by up to 2.2x; CoW copies only one block
examples.source: blog: 'cutting their memory usage by up to 55%. This can translate into up to 2.2x improvement in throughput'; arXiv: 'This involves only copying one block of data.'

examples.claim: enable_prefix_caching default True; SitePoint: APC reuses KV blocks of a shared system prompt, skipping redundant prefill and cutting TTFT, magnitude workload-dependent
examples.source: cache.py L260; SitePoint: 'APC reduces time-to-first-token by skipping redundant prefill computation. The magnitude depends on how large the shared prefix is'.

examples.claim: Illustrative budget: 2,048 tokens, 60 decodes leave 1,988; a 3,000-token prompt takes 1,988 now and 1,012 next iteration
examples.source: Labelled '가상의 숫자'; arithmetic 2,048-60=1,988, 3,000-1,988=1,012, 60+1,012=1,072 correct; chunking per enable_chunked_prefill docstring.

examples.claim: scheduler_reserve_full_isl (default True) checks the full input length fits in the KV cache before admitting, preventing over-admission and thrashing with chunked prefill
4 warps over 6 blocks: warp 0 takes blocks 0 and 4, warp 1 blocks 1 and 5, warps 2/3 one each; FP16 with THREAD_GROUP_SIZE 2 gives VEC_SIZE 4 and V_VEC_SIZE 8
Paper kernels show 20–26% higher attention-kernel latency than FasterTransformer, confined to the attention operator
examples.source: arXiv §7.1: 'this leads to 20–26% higher attention kernel latency, compared to the highly-optimized FasterTransformer implementation. We believe the overhead is small as it only affects the attention operator but not the other operators in the model, such as Linear.'

examples.claim: Single KV cache manager in the central scheduler; workers share the mapping, same physical block IDs, each storing only its heads' KV cache
examples.source: arXiv §4.6: 'vLLM features a single KV cache manager within the centralized scheduler ... Different GPU workers share the manager, as well as the mapping from logical blocks to physical blocks ... each GPU worker only stores a portion of the KV cache for its corresponding attention heads.' The 16-head/2-GPU split is the post's illustration.

examples.claim: Default binaries compiled with CUDA 12.9; CUDA 12.8 and 13.0 builds also published; --torch-backend=cu126 or UV_TORCH_BACKEND=cu126 pick a backend
examples.source: gpu.cuda.inc.md L53 'compiled with CUDA 12.9 ... We also provide vLLM binaries compiled with CUDA 12.8, 13.0'; quickstart.md L33.

examples.claim: VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE in GiB, default 0 means no override; per TP rank memory = weight shard + this value, exceeding a NUMA node kills the worker with exitcode 9; legacy, use --kv-cache-memory-bytes
--cap-add SYS_NICE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined is the least-privilege way to keep NUMA binding
examples.source: cpu.md L329-L336: '--security-opt seccomp=unconfined ... Actually, seccomp=unconfined bypasses the seccomp for container, if it's unacceptable, you can customize your own seccomp profile ... add migrate_pages to SCMP_ACT_ALLOW'. The docs present unconfined as a broad bypass; the narrow option is the custom profile. The post's next sentence admits the bypass, contradicting '최소 권한'. (Same defect as v16 L540.)

examples.claim: OneSource table: SGLang's 약점·운영 부담 is '특별한 운영 부담 없음(일반적인 배포 방식)', TGI's likewise
examples.source: OneSource 'Watch out for' column: SGLang 'Narrower hardware scope and community than vLLM'; TGI 'Throughput generally trails in published studies; development pace has lagged'. 'Plain deployment' is the source's operational-profile row; placing it in the 약점 column drops both engines' stated weaknesses.

off_sample_findings.source: Writer's inference (hedged '여지가 있습니다'); the cited buildmvpfast post's own low-concurrency data (TGI TTFT p50 0.18 s vs vLLM 0.24 s at 25 users) is not mentioned.
